cards.title: What is State?
cards.content:
State is an instance of React Component Class can be defined as an object of a set of observable properties that control the behavior of the component.

Unlike props, state is managed and updated within the component itself.

options.text: Props are mutable and managed inside the component.
State is mutable and managed inside the component.
State is passed from parent to child and cannot be changed.
Props and state are identical in functionality.

cards.title: The useState Hook
cards.content:
The useState hook lets you add React state to functional components.

import { useState } from 'react';

function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>{count}</button>
}

content.text: To declare a state variable in a functional component, we use the [blank] hook.

cards.title: Order the Steps to Use State

steps.text: Call useState inside the functional component with an initial value
Destructure the current state variable and the setter function
Use the setter function inside an event handler to update the state
